thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: P0 - Elevated 5xx error rate in /api/v1/generate (us-east1). Automated alert: error_rate > 5% for 3m, latency spike > 500ms. Pager: @sam (oncall) :rotating_light:

sam (oncall): I’m on it. Initial glance — Grafana shows 502/504 spike starting ~2m ago. Any deploys in last 30m?

mira (eng-oncall): I see a recent rollout of envoy route config at 14:22 UTC by joel, version envoy-route-v3. It introduced new retry_policy and per-route circuit_breaker defaults.

joel (infra): Confirmed. I rolled out a config tweak to move retries to upstream for certain routes, hoping to smooth transient 5xx. Did a canary but looks like traffic was bumped.

rachel (sre): Traffic pattern: heavy prefix fanout to model-host clusters. The retries are causing increased load on backend (model-hosts) which returns 502 under pressure -> retry loop. Dashboard: request rate steady but service error rate went from 0.8% to 9.6% in 3m.

luis (support): Customer impact: multiple customer slack threads reporting failed in-prod requests, some timeouts in streaming sessions. We have 12 active customer tickets citing generation failures.

anya (product): Any region isolation? Is this global or limited to us-east1?

monitoring-bot: Alert details: metric_id=api.errors.5xx, region=us-east1, ratio=0.096, window=5m. Top downstream errors: model-host-03 (502), model-host-07 (504).

sam (oncall): Ok plan: 1) Disable route-level retries immediately 2) Re-evaluate circuit breaker thresholds 3) If needed, rollback envoy-route-v3 4) Communicate to customers. Assign tasks: joel revert retry policy, mira validate config, rachel monitor.

joel (infra): Applying patch now. Command: 
```kubectl get configmap envoy-route-config -n infra -o yaml | yq eval '.data.route.yaml' - > /tmp/route.yaml
# remove retry_policy section for /api/v1/generate
yq eval 'del(.virtual_hosts[0].routes[] | select(.match.prefix=="/api/v1/generate") .retry_policy)' /tmp/route.yaml -i
kubectl create configmap envoy-route-config -n infra --from-file=route.yaml=/tmp/route.yaml -o yaml --dry-run=client | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl rollout restart ds/envoy -n infra
```

mira (eng-oncall): Noted. I’ll keep an eye on steady state and tail errors. If restart causes flaps we can do a staged restart by node.
monitoring-bot: Configmap apply succeeded; envoy daemonset restart triggered across 6 nodes.

rachel (sre): Early signals: error rate dropping from 9.6% -> 6.1% in 1 minute. Latency still slightly high (p50 320ms -> 410ms). Continue watching.

sam (oncall): Good. If we see <2% 5xx in 10m we can mark mitigated. Also need postmortem. Capture root cause and action items.

joel (infra): While removing retries I also noticed circuit_breakers configured with conservative max_connections=100, max_pending=50 for model-host cluster. That may be causing rapid 502s when retry storms occur. We should relax limits as a follow-up.

mira (eng-oncall): Can we do a quick tweak: increase per-host max_connections to 300 and max_pending to 200 for now? That should reduce immediate 5xx pressure. I can apply a targeted CDS update to model-host cluster.

joel (infra): Doing targeted CDS patch. Command snippet: 
```# patch envoy cluster settings
kubectl -n infra exec -it envoy-ctrl -- curl -X POST http://localhost:9901/cluster_manager?patch -d @patch.json
# patch.json increases common_lb_config and circuit_breaker thresholds for cluster model-host-cluster
```

monitoring-bot: CDS patch applied to control plane; data-plane config pushed to 4/6 nodes.

rachel (sre): Post-CDS: 5xx fell to 1.9% within 90s. p95 latency normalized. No further traffic spikes.

sam (oncall): Marking incident mitigated and paging resolved. Next: communicate to customers, perform controlled rollback of envoy-route-v3 to merge safer retry semantics, and add a guard in rollout pipeline to limit retry changes in high fanout routes.

luis (support): I'll post a note to affected customers: brief incident summary, mitigation steps, and ETA for full RCA.

anya (product): Also log which customers hit errors and whether SLA credit applies. We need to check contract thresholds.

mira (eng-oncall): Root-cause hypothesis to capture in postmortem: route-level retries enabled caused amplified load on model backend under high concurrency. Circuit breaker thresholds were too low to absorb the retry storm, leading to cascading 502/504. Canary rollout allowed wider exposure due to mis-sized canary (20% traffic).

rachel (sre): Action items (short-term): 1) Add rate-limiter before retries for high-fanout endpoints 2) Add a pre-deploy smoke test that simulates retry storms 3) Reduce canary weight for sentinel config changes to 5% 4) Increase circuit breaker defaults for model-host clusters 5) Update runbook to include 'disable retries' quick command.

joel (infra): Will open infra PR to revert retry_policy defaults and update helm chart to expose circuit_breaker tunables. Also add rollout guard: block retry_policy changes without explicit approval.

mira (eng-oncall): Scheduling follow-up: I’ll run a synthetic test to reproduce and validate fix in staging.

rachel (sre): Postmortem owner: mira. Target publish by EOD tomorrow.

incident-bot: Incident resolved and annotated. Incident ID: INC-2026-0516-01. Severity: P0 -> mitigated. Linking to ticket queue.

sam (oncall): Final notes: keep monitoring for 24h for regressions; if any spike recurs, escalate to oncall + infra immediate. Thanks everyone for quick responses. :thumbsup: 

luis (support): Sent customer messages with incident summary and link to status page.

anya (product): Thanks — please coordinate any customer follow-ups with me.

monitoring-bot: Post-incident metrics snapshot: peak 5xx 9.6% -> mitigated to 0.8% in 7m; affected requests ~28k in window; top region us-east1.

rachel (sre): Adding notes to runbook: sample quick commands for disabling retries and rolling back route-config.

mira (eng-oncall): Uploading the small config diff I applied to the incident doc. Snippet of problematic config that caused the loop: 
```# problematic route fragment
- match: { prefix: "/api/v1/generate" }
  route: { cluster: model-host-cluster }
  retry_policy:
    retry_on: 5xx,connect,refused_stream
    num_retries: 3
    per_try_timeout: 10s
```
Recommended safe config: 
```# safer approach
- match: { prefix: "/api/v1/generate" }
  route: { cluster: model-host-cluster }
  retry_policy: { retry_on: connect,refused_stream, num_retries: 1, retry_host_predicate: [ "secondary-hosts-only" ] }
```

sam (oncall): Good. Closing thread but keep the incident doc updated with timelines and exact deploy diffs.
